1.title: Automate Data Processing
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Automate Data Processing. This module covers the task statement: automate data processing by using a w s services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Orchestrate pipelines with Amazon M W A A (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow) and A W S Step Functions and troubleshoot managed workflows. Call S D K s (software development kit) to use A W S features from code. Use Amazon E M R (Elastic MapReduce), Amazon Redshift and A W S Glue features to process data. Consume and maintain data A P I s. Prepare data for transformation with A W S Glue DataBrew and SageMaker Unified Studio. Query data with Amazon Athena.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight Keeps the Pipeline Running
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight Keeps the Pipeline Running. The nightly pipeline runs unattended and finishes at five:zero. Last night a D A G (directed acyclic graph) disappeared, a Step Functions run failed and a Glue job never started. The on-call engineer needs to know where to look. Your job: automate the runs and fix them fast.

1.title: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows
1.text: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows. Amazon M W A A. Where to look when it breaks: CloudWatch Logs for the scheduler, D A G processing, worker, webserver and task logs; the Airflow U I; the D A G files and requirements.txt in S three. Common causes: D A G not showing: a syntax or import error, file not yet synced from S three, or a missing plugin or requirement; tasks stuck in queued: not enough workers (raise the maximum workers or the environment class); access denied: the execution role lacks permission; cannot reach the internet or a service: V P C (Virtual Private Cloud) route, N A T (network address translation) gateway or V P C endpoint missing.

1.title: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued
1.text: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued. A W S Step Functions. Where to look when it breaks: Execution history and graph view (which state failed and its input and output); CloudWatch Logs (needed for Express). Common causes: States.TaskFailed (the service call failed), States.Timeout (task or heartbeat timed out), missing I A M (Identity and Access Management) permission on the execution role (especially for.sync and callback patterns), bad input path, no Retry or Catch.

1.title: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued
1.text: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued. A W S Glue workflows. Where to look when it breaks: The workflow graph (dynamic view), each job run's logs and error message, trigger state. Common causes: A trigger is not activated, a dependent job only runs if a trigger started the chain, workflow concurrency limit reached, job role or connection problem. EventBridge. Where to look when it breaks: Rule metrics, dead-letter queue of a target, CloudTrail. Common causes: Event pattern does not match, target permission missing, target throttled. Automate recovery: Retry with backoff, Catch to a fallback state, alarms that notify, idempotent steps so a rerun from the failed step is safe.

1.title: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued
1.text: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued. Operate: version D A G s and state machines, alarm on failure counts and duration, keep runbooks.

1.title: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued
1.text: Orchestrating and Troubleshooting Managed Workflows, continued. The figure shows this: Troubleshooting a managed workflow: find the failed step, read its logs, classify the cause (code, permission, network, capacity), fix it and rerun from that step. Exam tip: "An Airflow task never starts and sits in queued" to add workers (raise max workers or environment class). "A Step Functions.sync task fails with access denied" to add the integrated service's permissions to the state machine role.

1.title: Calling SDKs from Code
1.text: Calling S D K s from Code. An A W S S D K (Python boto three, Java, JavaScript, Go and more) lets code call A W S services: start Glue jobs, run Athena queries, read S three, put Kinesis records. Credentials: never hard-code keys: run code with an I A M role (Lambda execution role, Glue job role, E C two (Elastic Compute Cloud) or task role); the S D K picks up temporary credentials automatically; secrets come from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store. Built-in resilience: the S D K retries with exponential backoff on throttling and server errors; tune maximum attempts and timeouts. Pagination: list and query calls return pages; use paginators or next-token loops.

1.title: Calling SDKs from Code, continued
1.text: Calling S D K s from Code, continued. Waiters: poll until a resource reaches a state (for example an Athena query is S U C C E E D E D). Asynchronous calls: many data A P I s start work and return an I D (Athena StartQueryExecution, Redshift Data A P I ExecuteStatement); poll the status (or use events) and then fetch results. Idempotency tokens (ClientToken) make retries safe for operations that create or change things. Region and endpoint settings, V P C endpoints for private access. Exam tip: "A Lambda function calls Athena and must wait for the query" to StartQueryExecution, then poll GetQueryExecution (or use Step Functions.sync) and read results with GetQueryResults.

1.title: Using Service Features to Process Data
1.text: Using Service Features to Process Data. Amazon E M R. Steps (a unit of work on a cluster), auto-termination of idle clusters, managed scaling, bootstrap actions, E M R Serverless (automatic capacity), notebooks (E M R Studio). Amazon Redshift. Stored procedures, scheduled queries (query editor schedules), materialized views with auto refresh, auto-copy from S three, Redshift Data A P I, zero-E T L (extract, transform, load) integrations that replicate from Aurora, R D S (Relational Database Service) and DynamoDB, streaming ingestion, automatic table optimization and concurrency scaling. A W S Glue. Triggers and workflows, job bookmarks, auto scaling, Data Quality rules, Glue Studio visual E T L, interactive sessions, DynamicFrames, pushdown predicates, Flex execution.

1.title: Using Service Features to Process Data, continued
1.text: Using Service Features to Process Data, continued. Amazon Athena. C T A S (create table as select) and insert into for E T L, views, workgroups, federated queries, result reuse. Pick the built-in feature before custom code: it is cheaper to run and easier to maintain.

1.title: Consuming and Maintaining Data APIs
1.text: Consuming and Maintaining Data A P I s. Consume an A P I: authenticate (I A M, tokens, keys in Secrets Manager), paginate, respect rate limits, retry on four twenty-nine and five hundred series (Module one). Maintain an A P I you publish with Amazon A P I Gateway:; Stages (dev, test, prod) and deployments; version the A P I path or header; deprecate old versions gradually; Throttling and quotas (default ten thousand requests per second per account per Region with a burst) and usage plans with A P I keys; Caching of responses to protect the backend; Authorization: I A M, Amazon Cognito user pools, Lambda authorizers; Monitoring: CloudWatch metrics (four hundred series, five hundred series, latency, count) and access logs; alarms on error rates.

1.title: Consuming and Maintaining Data APIs, continued
1.text: Consuming and Maintaining Data A P I s, continued. Redshift Data A P I and Athena A P I are data A P I s you consume from code without managing drivers or servers.

1.title: Preparing Data for Transformation
1.text: Preparing Data for Transformation. The figure shows this: A W S Glue DataBrew: connect a dataset, profile it, build a recipe of visual transforms, and run a recipe job that writes cleaned data to S three. A W S Glue DataBrew is a visual, no-code data preparation tool: datasets, profile jobs (statistics and quality), projects (interactive grid), recipes (ordered steps; over two hundred fifty prebuilt transformations), and recipe jobs (run on a schedule or on demand, write to S three or other targets).

2.title: Preparing Data for Transformation, continued
2.text: Preparing Data for Transformation, continued. Typical steps: remove or fill nulls, standardize formats and case, split or merge columns, filter, mask or hash sensitive fields, join and union, change types. Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is an integrated workspace for data, analytics and A I (artificial intelligence): notebooks, visual E T L with Glue, S Q L, catalog access and Amazon Q help, organized in domains and projects (Module fourteen). Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler also prepares data visually for M L (Module eleven). Exam tip: "Analysts without coding skills clean and standardize data and run it on a schedule" to A W S Glue DataBrew.

2.title: Querying Data with Amazon Athena
2.text: Querying Data with Amazon Athena. Athena is a serverless, interactive S Q L query service over data in S three (through the Glue Data Catalog); you pay for the data scanned, so partition, compress and use Parquet. Workgroups separate teams and workloads: per-workgroup query result location, encryption, data-scanned limits (cost control), query limits and CloudWatch metrics. Federated queries use Lambda-based data source connectors to query R D S, DynamoDB, Redshift, OpenSearch and on-premises sources in place. C T A S (create table as select) and insert into turn Athena into an E T L engine (convert to Parquet, partition, compact).

2.title: Querying Data with Amazon Athena, continued
2.text: Querying Data with Amazon Athena, continued. Views save queries; prepared statements and parameterized queries are reusable; query result reuse avoids re-running identical queries. Query timeout: about thirty minutes for S Q L queries by default (adjustable); results are written to S three. Athena notebooks with Apache Spark are in Module eleven. Exam tip: "Control cost per team in Athena" to separate workgroups with data-scanned limits. "Query a database and S three together without moving data" to Athena federated query.

2.title: Lambda, Events and Schedulers
2.text: Lambda, Events and Schedulers. A W S Lambda automates glue steps: start a Glue job or crawler when a file arrives, validate or move files, call an A P I, fan out work, react to a CloudWatch alarm, clean up resources. Event-driven automation: S three events, EventBridge rules, S Q S (Simple Queue Service), S N S (Simple Notification Service), DynamoDB Streams, Kinesis invoke Lambda (Modules one and two). EventBridge routes events and schedules work: rules with patterns, Pipes, and Scheduler (cron, rate, one-time, time zones, flexible windows) (Modules one and four). Operate it: dead-letter queues or destinations, retries, idempotent handlers, alarms on errors and throttles, reserved concurrency to protect downstream systems (Module five).

2.title: Lambda, Events and Schedulers, continued
2.text: Lambda, Events and Schedulers, continued. Choose the trigger: time (Scheduler), event (EventBridge or S three), completion of a step (Step Functions, Glue triggers). Exam tip: "Run a Glue job every night" to EventBridge Scheduler (or a Glue scheduled trigger); "run it when a file lands" to S three event to EventBridge rule or Lambda.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. M W A A troubleshooting: CloudWatch scheduler or D A G-processing or worker logs; D A G missing equals syntax or import or requirements; queued tasks equals more workers. Step Functions troubleshooting: Execution history and graph; States.TaskFailed, States.Timeout; I A M role for.sync or callback. Glue workflows: Graph and job run logs; trigger must be activated; concurrency limits. S D K: I A M roles, no hard-coded keys; auto retry with backoff; paginators, waiters, ClientToken; async data A P I s (poll). Service features: E M R steps or auto-termination or scaling or Serverless; Redshift stored procedures, scheduled queries, auto-refresh M V s (materialized view), zero-E T L. A P I Gateway: Stages, versions, throttling (ten thousand rps default), usage plans, caching, authorizers, CloudWatch. DataBrew: Visual, two hundred fifty plus transforms, profile to recipe to job; SageMaker Unified Studio for notebooks and visual E T L.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A new D A G file was uploaded to the S three bucket of an Amazon M W A A environment but it does not appear in the Airflow U I. Where should the engineer look first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. D A G processing logs show parse errors; a missing D A G usually has a syntax or import error, or a missing requirement or plugin.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Airflow tasks stay in the queued state for a long time while the environment's workers are fully busy. What is the most direct fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Queued tasks mean there is not enough worker capacity; raising maximum workers or the environment class adds capacity.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A Lambda function starts an Amazon Athena query and must use the results. What is the correct pattern? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Athena queries run asynchronously: start the query, wait for success, then fetch the results (or use Step Functions with the Run a Job pattern).

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Finance analysts with no coding skills need to clean and standardize C S V files and run the same steps every night. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. DataBrew provides visual preparation with reusable recipes and scheduled jobs for non-coders.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Two teams share an A W S account and Athena. The company wants a separate query result location and a monthly data-scanned limit for each team. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Workgroups isolate query results, encryption settings and cost controls such as data-scanned limits per workload or team.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Select two. Which two practices make an automated pipeline easier to recover after a failure? The five options are on the screen. The answers are C and D. Idempotent steps allow rerunning from the failed point, and retries, catches and alarms handle and surface failures.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all six answers. Question one: B. Question two: C. Question three: A. Question four: A. Question five: C. Question six: C and D. In the next module, we continue the course.
